dimensional_ladder.theorem: I(0,0)|_D = sqrt(pi)*Gamma((D-1)/2)/Gamma(D/2) = Vol(S^{D-1})/Vol(S^{D-2}) for all D

r_target_connection.interpretation: The GRUT quotient target R is the square root of the AJ integral evaluated ONE DIMENSION HIGHER than the Gate 3 computation.

d4_coincidence.theorem: At n=4 ONLY: Vol(S4)/Vol(S3) = lambda_1(S4)/lambda_1(S3) = 4/3 = R_target^2
d4_coincidence.uniqueness: The coincidence Vol(S^n)/Vol(S^{n-1}) = n/(n-1) (spectral gap ratio) holds at n=4 because Gamma(2)/Gamma(5/2) = 1/(3sqrt(pi)/4) = 4/(3sqrt(pi)), and Vol(S4)/Vol(S3) = sqrt(pi)*Gamma(2)/Gamma(5/2) = 4/3 = spectral ratio. This simplification is dimension-specific.
d4_coincidence.physical_interpretation: Four is the unique dimension where the volume-projection and spectral-gap sector coupling mechanisms give IDENTICAL ratios.  Both independently constrain g_cosmo/g_final = sqrt(4/3) = R_target.

candidates_scored.name: volume_projection
candidates_scored.label: Volume-projection coupling
candidates_scored.description: Cosmological sector couples with weight sqrt(Vol(S4)), final sector with weight sqrt(Vol(S3)).  Ratio: sqrt(Vol(S4)/Vol(S3)) = sqrt(4/3). Physical: sector projectors have different sphere-volume footprints.  This is purely geometric (no free parameters).
candidates_scored.requires: Identify which sector projects onto S4 footprint and which onto S3

candidates_scored.name: spectral_gap
candidates_scored.label: Spectral-gap coupling
candidates_scored.description: Sector couplings are set by the first nonzero eigenvalue of the Laplacian on the corresponding sphere: g_cosmo ~ sqrt(lambda_1(S4))=2, g_final ~ sqrt(lambda_1(S3))=sqrt(3).  Ratio: sqrt(4/3) = R_target. Unique to D=4: only at n=4 does Vol(S^n)/Vol(S^{n-1}) = lambda_1(S^n)/lambda_1(S^{n-1}).
candidates_scored.requires: Verify that sector couplings in GRUT action are set by S4 and S3 spectral gaps

candidates_scored.name: dimensional_ladder
candidates_scored.label: Dimensional-ladder coupling (D=4 vs D=5 AJ integrals)
candidates_scored.description: The AJ dimensional ladder gives I(0,0)|_D = Vol(S^{D-1})/Vol(S^{D-2}). At D=5: I(0,0) = 4/3 = R^2.  Therefore R = sqrt(I(0,0)|_{D=5}). If the cosmological sector uses the D=4 loop (pi/2) and the final sector uses the D=5 loop (4/3) with a half-power weighting, this gives R = sqrt(4/3). The D=4 and D=5 integrals are adjacent rungs of the same ladder — no free parameters.
candidates_scored.requires: Identify whether the GRUT final sector involves a D=5 dimensional extension

candidates_scored.name: equal_coupling
candidates_scored.label: Equal sector coupling (g_cosmo = g_final)
candidates_scored.description: Both sectors receive the same scalar-loop coupling.  The shared pi/2 normalization cancels and R = 1.  This CONTRADICTS R = sqrt(4/3) and is included as a consistency check.
candidates_scored.requires: Nothing — trivial default; fails because R != 1

candidates_scored.name: euler_density_normalization
candidates_scored.label: Euler-density projection normalization
candidates_scored.description: The Gauss-Bonnet integrand E4 on the unit S4 equals 24 (constant). The Gauss-Bonnet integral: int_{S4} E4 d^4x = 64*pi^2 = 32*pi^2 * chi(S4). The sector coupling ratio from the Euler-density projection: g_Euler/g_vol = sqrt(int E4 / Vol(S4)) = sqrt(64*pi^2 / (8*pi^2/3)) = sqrt(24). This gives sqrt(24) != sqrt(4/3), so Euler-density normalization alone does not reproduce R_target without additional structure.
candidates_scored.requires: Identify additional projection structure that maps sqrt(24) to sqrt(4/3)

candidates_scored.name: hand_tuned
candidates_scored.label: Hand-tuned sector ratio
candidates_scored.description: g_cosmo/g_final = sqrt(4/3) is inserted as a free parameter to match R. This is circular (it assumes the answer) and lacks geometric basis.

candidates_scored.name: ctp_response_weighting
candidates_scored.label: CTP response-sector weighting
candidates_scored.description: If the GRUT action has a non-Euclidean (Lorentzian or de Sitter) ingredient that breaks the S4 CTP symmetry, one sector might acquire a response-type (retarded/advanced) weight relative to the other.  This would require identifying a specific CTP mechanism not present in pure Euclidean S4.
candidates_scored.requires: Identify non-Euclidean ingredient in the GRUT CTP action

summary.blocking_question: Does the GRUT CTP action assign sector couplings via the sphere-volume ladder (C1), spectral gaps (C2), or the D=5 AJ integral (C3)?  All three are equivalent geometrically; the distinction is which sector couples to S4 and which to S3 (or D=5).
